speaker: bayo
text: (on the phone) I don show dem everything. Tomorrow, the press go hear am.

speaker: bayo
text: Dayo. Take this phone. Run. Go Mama. No look back.

speaker: voice
text: Bayo, you for just collect the money. Make una finish am.

speaker: voice
text: No witness.

speaker: sego
text: Sabi! You dey sleep for road? Obalende people don full ground!

speaker: dayo
text: I dey here, I dey here. Make we hustle.

speaker: sego
text: Obalende! Obalende! Enter with your change o!

speaker: passenger
text: Oga, I no get ₦200 change. Drop me for next bus stop.

speaker: sego
text: Madam, change na your own wahala, no be ours!

speaker: herbal
text: Malaria, ulcer, bad luck: one bottle cure all! Five hundred naira only!

speaker: sego
text: Oga herbal, abeg no sell bad luck inside my bus. We get enough.

speaker: sego
text: Sabi, see bag for back seat. Somebody forget am.

speaker: dayo
text: UNILAG ID card. Tolu Adeyemi. This girl na Kemi classmate.

speaker: sego
text: As our elders say... I no remember wetin dem say, but e go make sense later.

speaker: wire
text: Driver! Today ticket na double. Chairman orders.

speaker: dayo
text: Double? I pay this morning.

speaker: wire
text: Morning na morning, evening na evening. Pay, or we scatter that bus.

speaker: dayo
text: Then come scatter am.

speaker: voice
text: ...No witness.

speaker: sego
text: Sabi! Your hand! Ah, small wahala, small wahala. Make we comot here!

speaker: dayo
text: One chance bus. Not today.

speaker: amaka
text: Thank you. Thank you. I sell aso-ebi for Balogun market. I just enter the wrong bus.

speaker: dayo
text: Aso-ebi seller wey dey carry camera?

speaker: amaka
text: Please. Forget wetin you see.

speaker: dayo
text: Lagos na place of secrets, madam. I no see anything.

speaker: kongi
text: Sabi. The boy wey beat my boys. Sit down.

speaker: kongi
text: I need driver wey get liver. ₦500,000 for one job: a special load of rice to the Seme border.

speaker: kongi
text: You like am? Gift from a big man. Lagos na place of gifts, Sabi.

speaker: choice
text: I'm in. (Stay close to Kongi.)

speaker: choice
text: ₦500,000 na money. I'm in.

speaker: wire
text: Chairman say make I give you this. Half now, half when you come back.

speaker: obinna
text: (on the phone) Dayo, my son. I hear you dey move with those park people.

speaker: obinna
text: Stay away from them, you hear? Think of your sister. Think of Mama.

speaker: dayo
text: I hear you, Uncle Obi.

speaker: wire
text: (radio) Follow the escort. No stop for anybody. Customs see you, na your own palava.

speaker: dayo
text: Rice no dey breathe.

speaker: tolu
text: Please... please. They said we were going to Cotonou.

speaker: tolu
text: God bless you. Tell Kemi I'm alive.

speaker: dayo
text: You go tell am yourself.

speaker: dayo
text: Kongi! You and me need to talk.

speaker: kongi
text: Sabi? You come here to—

speaker: kongi
text: (bleeding) Dem no come for me. Dem come make you look like say na you.

speaker: hauwa
text: Oladayo Balogun. Hands where I can see them. You are under arrest.

speaker: dayo
text: I just saved this man's life!

speaker: hauwa
text: Then you will have plenty to tell the judge.

speaker: obinna
text: (on the phone) Don't worry, my daughter. I will handle it.

speaker: president
text: New boy! Your people bring food? Na me dey chop first. Na me be president for here.

speaker: boy
text: Please... na my mama food. I never chop since yesterday.

speaker: president
text: You dey argue with president? Oya, bring am.

speaker: dayo
text: Leave the boy alone.

speaker: boy
text: Thank you, sir. God go bless you.

speaker: inmate
text: (from the corner) That one na soldier. See as he dey fight.

speaker: hauwa
text: Balogun. Up. Quietly.

speaker: hauwa
text: I know you freed those girls at Seme. The rice sacks. The church in Badagry.

speaker: dayo
text: So why am I in this cell?

speaker: hauwa
text: Because somebody wanted you here. My brother Sadiq vanished from Oshodi park three years ago. Nobody looked for him. I am looking.

speaker: hauwa
text: My deal: I stage your escape tonight. You go back inside, close to the people who move people. You tell me everything.

speaker: choice
text: "Get me out."

speaker: choice
text: "For the girls. Not for you."

speaker: hauwa
text: Through the yard. The gate is unlocked for five minutes. Run, and don't look back.

speaker: hauwa
text: Those are not my men! Take this!

speaker: hauwa
text: More coming! Use the pickup for cover!

speaker: hauwa
text: (breathing hard) Somebody in my own command sent them. They were going to shoot you "while escaping".

speaker: hauwa
text: Go. Call me on this number. Nobody else.

speaker: dayo
text: And if your somebody finds me first?

speaker: hauwa
text: Then run faster.

speaker: amaka
text: No more aso-ebi seller. I work for The Lagos Ledger. I've been following people who vanish from motor parks for a year.

speaker: dayo
text: You could have told me on the bridge.

speaker: amaka
text: You could have been one of them. This is Bigz. He can trace the phones from the Seme convoy.

speaker: bigz
text: Sabi! Correct guy. My fee is small: some Allen Avenue boys stole my laptop. Everything is inside. Help me collect am back.

speaker: bigz
text: Look, see am there! The one in the blue shirt!

speaker: thief
text: Wahala! Na Bigz!

speaker: thief
text: Oga, no vex! Na dem send me!

speaker: bigz
text: My baby! Give me two minutes.

speaker: bigz
text: Your Seme numbers... every one of them pings the same place on weekends. An event centre in Lekki.

speaker: amaka
text: Saturday is the senator's daughter's wedding there. Every big man in Lagos will be inside.

speaker: dayo
text: Then we're going to a wedding.

speaker: amaka
text: Matching aso-ebi. Smile like you're family. Spray money, dance when the drummer calls, and keep away from the aunties.

speaker: amaka
text: The back room. That's where the big men meet. We need a photo of whoever goes in.

speaker: dayo
text: And the aunties?

speaker: amaka
text: They know everybody's face. Everybody's.

speaker: wire
text: ...Na who dey for window? NA YOU! SABI!

speaker: amaka
text: Run!

speaker: amaka
text: (leaning out of the back with Dayo's pistol) Drive! I've got the camera and I've got their tyres!

speaker: amaka
text: Wire. Kongi's lieutenant. Taking the senator's money.

speaker: dayo
text: So it's Kongi.

speaker: bigz
text: (phone) Wire's phone is in Makoko. One house, far end, near the open water. It hasn't moved since morning.

speaker: captive
text: Please... don't kill us.

speaker: dayo
text: I'm here to take you home. Who brought you?

speaker: captive
text: The men say the Chairman of Oshodi go collect us. Tonight.

speaker: wire
text: (outside) Burn am! Burn everything!

speaker: dayo
text: ...I'm fine. Go. Go!

speaker: mama_agba
text: (phone) Dayo? You're bleeding? Listen to me. Go to Abeokuta. Baba Fakunle. Go now.

speaker: fakunle
text: So this is Bayo's son. Lie down. The bullet is out; now the fever must go.

speaker: fakunle
text: The hand that washes your face is the same hand that dirtied it.

speaker: dayo
text: Riddles, Baba?

speaker: fakunle
text: Your father was not killed over union politics. He found something, and he was going to the press. That is all Ifá will say today.

speaker: voice
text: No witness.

speaker: dayo
text: ...I know that hand.

speaker: fakunle
text: Go back to Lagos, son of Bayo. And look closely at those who love you.

speaker: dayo
text: Kongi. Tonight we finish this.

speaker: rasheed
text: (radio, Kongi's boys) Sabi dey come for Papa! Stop am for bridge!

speaker: kongi
text: (drops his gun) Sabi... Listen to me. I no kill your papa.

speaker: kongi
text: I carry your papa body for my hand. This stick? Dem dash me am one year after. Make e look like say na me.

speaker: kongi
text: The man wey dash me na—

speaker: rasheed
text: PAPA! You kill my papa! Sabi, you are a dead man!

speaker: dayo
text: Rasheed. I need to talk to you. I didn't—

speaker: rasheed
text: (gun to Dayo's head) You come here? To my papa burial?

speaker: imam
text: Not here. Not today. Put it down, my son.

speaker: rasheed
text: ...Eight days. After my papa Fidau prayer, I go find you. Run, Sabi.

speaker: dayo
text: Eight days.

speaker: aide
text: Listen. The opposition wards: the polling units by the stadium. Carry the boxes to the bus. Nobody gets hurt if nobody is stupid.

speaker: aide
text: Fifty thousand each. Cash. Today.

speaker: choice
text: Swap them for marked decoys, and film it all for Amaka (stealth)

speaker: choice
text: Snatch them with the boys (big payout, the senator's people trust you)

speaker: amaka
text: (earpiece) The decoys are in the blue bag. Swap the boxes in the truck and keep the phone recording.

speaker: aide
text: (counting notes into Dayo's hand) Good work. Oga Ọkpụ say make we take care of you.

speaker: dayo
text: Oga who?

speaker: aide
text: Don't worry yourself. Big man. Very big man.

speaker: sego
text: Sabi... my mama. The doctors say surgery today today, or... I no get the money. I no get anything.

speaker: dayo
text: Take it. All of it.

speaker: sego
text: (crying) Sabi, na you be my brother. Anything. Anything.

speaker: doctor
text: We'll take her from here. Theatre is ready.

speaker: sego
text: God bless you, Sabi.

speaker: bigz
text: (phone) The cattle trucks leave Lagos full and come back empty. This week they're in Kano, hiding in the Durbar crowds.

speaker: hauwa
text: My cousin Musa. He rides for the emir.

speaker: musa
text: Can you ride, Lagos boy?

speaker: dayo
text: I can drive anything.

speaker: musa
text: A horse is not a danfo. Hold on with your knees.

speaker: sadiq
text: ...Hauwa?

speaker: hauwa
text: Sadiq. Sadiq! Allah, Sadiq!

speaker: sadiq
text: The buyers are foreigners. But the seller... an Igbo businessman. They call him Ọkpụ.

speaker: dayo
text: (to himself) Okoroba. I swore I'd never come back to these creeks.

speaker: bigz
text: (phone) The money goes through General Tonye's refineries. Find him.

speaker: tonye
text: Who send you here? You come to die?

speaker: tonye
text: ...Wait. Wait. I know this face.

speaker: tonye
text: Na you be the soldier wey refuse burn Okoroba. My mama still dey alive because of you.

speaker: tonye
text: Dem follow you! Oya, enter boat!

speaker: tonye
text: (watching the creek burn) Your senator na puppet. The man wey dey hold the rope dey Alaba. Na trader, not politician.

speaker: dayo
text: Uncle. They're coming for us. The ring, the senator... a trader in Alaba is behind it all.

speaker: obinna
text: (horrified) In MY market? Dayo... come here. Come here, my son.

speaker: obinna
text: Nobody touches my sister's children. I have a house in Festac. Take Mama and Kemi there tonight. Money, guns, anything.

speaker: kemi
text: Uncle Obi did all this for us? See, Dayo. Family.

speaker: mama_agba
text: (her iron box on her knees, as always) Sit, Dayo. For one night, let us be a family that is not afraid.

speaker: sego
text: I bring food! Jollof and chicken. How una dey?

speaker: kemi
text: Sego! Who told you we were here?

speaker: sego
text: (a beat) ...Sabi tell me now. Abi?

speaker: kemi
text: Dayo! The back door!

speaker: dayo
text: MAMA! No, no, no...

speaker: mama_agba
text: (pointing at her iron box) Wo ọwọ́ tó ń bọ́ ẹ... Look at the hand that feeds you...

speaker: hauwa
text: Dayo! Wait—

speaker: dayo
text: You! YOU!

speaker: dayo
text: He knew where we were. Only Sego knew.

speaker: sego
text: Sabi... Sabi, I fit explain—

speaker: sego
text: (through tears) Dem pay for my mama surgery! Then dem say the doctor go "make mistake" if I no tell them where you dey hide.

speaker: sego
text: I no know say dem go shoot Mama. I swear to God. I swear!

speaker: choice
text: Let him go. "Get out of Lagos."

speaker: choice
text: Mama is dead because of him.

speaker: dayo
text: Go. Get out of my sight. If you ever pray, pray for Mama.

speaker: sego
text: I go make am up to you. I swear, Sabi.

speaker: dayo
text: From Papa's phone. Mama, you kept it fifteen years...

speaker: bigz
text: Old card, old phone. Give me one hour.

speaker: voice
text: Bayo, you for just collect the money. Make una finish am. No witness.

speaker: voice
text: (in Igbo, to someone else) Ọ dị mma. Give Rasaki the stick next year. Let them look at him.

speaker: bigz
text: I ran the voice against every voice I have. Radio adverts too.

speaker: bigz
text: One match. Chief Obinna Nwankwo. "Ọkpụ of Alaba".

speaker: dayo
text: Uncle Obi.

speaker: neighbour
text: Sabi! Welcome o. How Mama? We never see am for market this week.

speaker: hauwa
text: I got the tip-off too late. I came to stop it. The raiders in uniform were CP Ladipo's men. My commissioner. He is on Ọkpụ's payroll.

speaker: hauwa
text: He has declared me wanted this morning.

speaker: dayo
text: So now we are both fugitives.

speaker: hauwa
text: Alliance of outcasts.

speaker: hauwa
text: Ladipo's unit! They followed me. Through the market, go!

speaker: hauwa
text: A city bus? Seriously?

speaker: dayo
text: I drive anything with wheels.

speaker: rasheed
text: You get mind. Talk your last talk.

speaker: dayo
text: Not my talk. My father's. Listen.

speaker: voice
text: Make una finish am. No witness... Give Rasaki the stick next year. Let them look at him.

speaker: rasheed
text: (lowering his gun) ...Na the same man kill both our papa.

speaker: rasheed
text: Oshodi dey with you, Sabi.

speaker: dayo
text: (in a masquerade attendant's raffia) Nobody looks twice at the man who walks behind a masquerade.

speaker: kemi
text: Dayo! Uncle Obi will kill them when he knows—

speaker: dayo
text: Kemi. It's him. Uncle Obi is Ọkpụ.

speaker: kemi
text: No. No, you're lying. He paid my fees. He—

speaker: obinna
text: (from the balcony) Kemi-Kemi! My Ada! Where are you going with that boy?

speaker: kemi
text: ...Uncle?

speaker: obinna
text: (to his men) Shoot the car.

speaker: kemi
text: (barely a whisper) It's true.

speaker: kemi
text: He'll be there. Before they both fly out.

speaker: dayo
text: Then so will we.

speaker: bigz
text: (radio) Three. Two. One.

speaker: dayo
text: (radio) The senator's gateman took the suya and the money. His generator is dead.

speaker: dayo
text: (radio) They're not leaving tomorrow. They're leaving tonight. Everybody, now!

speaker: amaka
text: (radio) LIVE: CP Ladipo is in handcuffs! Hauwa did it!

speaker: dayo
text: One more floor.

speaker: senator
text: (on his knees) Please! Please, I'm only a politician! It was Ọkpụ, it was all Ọkpụ!

speaker: dayo
text: Obinna?

speaker: senator
text: He's not on it. The yacht. The jetty. He said: "Tell my nephew I'll be waiting for him."

speaker: sego
text: (clutching his shoulder, laughing) Sabi... we don dey even.

speaker: dayo
text: Sego! You fool. You beautiful fool.

speaker: obinna
text: (the lion staff in his hand: he took it back from Kongi's grave) Your father was my brother too. He wanted to bring police into my business.

speaker: obinna
text: Lagos eats righteous men, Dayo. I fed your family for fifteen years. Your bus? Mine. Your sister's books? Mine.

speaker: obinna
text: You are standing on my money.

speaker: choice
text: Take the staff. The city's power passes to you.

speaker: choice
text: Drag him to shore. Hand him to Hauwa alive.

speaker: choice
text: Walk away. Leave him to the lagoon. Take Kemi and go.

speaker: kemi
text: Where are we going?

speaker: dayo
text: Across.

speaker: rasheed
text: Sabi, Oshodi need you.
